## Overview

Greeks, or Hellenes, are an ethnic group and nation native to Greece, Cyprus, southern Albania, Turkey, southern Italy, parts of Egypt, and other areas around the Eastern Mediterranean and the Black Sea. Greek communities have historically occupied the shores of the Mediterranean Sea and the Black Sea, while the Greek people have been concentrated especially around the Aegean Sea and the Ionian Sea. Greeks speak Greek, an independent branch of the Indo-European language family, and Greek has been spoken since the Bronze Age. Greek communities and institutions have contributed to visual arts, theatre, literature, philosophy, architecture, music, cuisine, science, and sports.

## Material culture

### Textile & pattern traditions

### Architecture

The sources mention Greek contributions to architecture. They identify Athens, Thessalonica, Alexandria, Smyrna, and Constantinople as cultural centres of the Greeks at various periods.

## Music & performance

The sources identify music as one of the fields to which the Greek people have contributed. Greek was used as a lingua franca across much of the Mediterranean world during the Hellenistic period and retained that position in Roman times.

## Dance & theatre

The sources state that the Greek people contributed to theatre and identify the works of Homer, including the *Iliad* and *Odyssey*, as central to Greek cultural history.

## Festivals & rituals

The Olympic Games in 776 BC are presented as a foundational event in the development of a common Hellenic identity. They translated the idea of common Hellenism among Greek tribes into a shared cultural experience, while Hellenism was primarily understood as a matter of common culture. The Oracle of Apollo at Delphi was established in the same period.

The sources describe the religious history of Greek communities across several periods. Ancient Greek religious practices continued in some regions into the Christian era, and southeastern Peloponnese remained pagan until well into the mid-Byzantine 10th century AD. The region of Tsakonia remained pagan until the ninth century. Later, Christianity became central to Greek identity, and most religious Greeks today are Christians officially registered with the Greek Orthodox Church.

## Foodways

The sources identify cuisine among the fields to which the Greek people have contributed.

## Oral tradition & literature

The Homeric epics, the *Iliad* and *Odyssey*, were accepted by the Greeks of classical antiquity as part of the Greek past and were associated with the heritage of the Mycenaean period. The works of Homer and Hesiod, including the *Theogony*, were written in the 8th century BC and became foundations of ancient Greek religion, ethos, history, and mythology.

The Greeks of classical antiquity idealized their Mycenaean ancestors as belonging to a heroic age associated with closeness to the gods and material wealth. The names of Mycenaean gods and goddesses, including Zeus, Poseidon, and Hades, became major figures of the Olympian Pantheon.

Greek literature was preserved and transmitted through Byzantine Greek scholarship. Byzantine grammarians carried ancient Greek grammatical and literary studies to the West during the 15th century, contributing to the Italian Renaissance. The Aristotelian philosophical tradition continued in the Greek world until the Fall of Constantinople in 1453.

## Language & religion

Greek forms its own branch within the Indo-European family of languages, the Hellenic. It is described as the oldest recorded living language, and its vocabulary has provided material for many languages, including English, and for international scientific nomenclature. Greek became a widely spoken lingua franca in the Mediterranean world from the 4th century BC and was used in the New Testament of the Christian Bible.

The sources describe several historical writing systems. In c. 1600 BC, the Mycenaean Greeks adopted a syllabic writing system from the Minoan civilization and developed Linear B, the earliest and oldest written evidence of Greek. The sources also credit the Byzantine Greek monks Cyril and Methodius with formalizing the first Slavic alphabet.

Most religious Greeks are Christians officially registered with the Greek Orthodox Church. Greek identity has historically combined Orthodox Christianity with the Homeric tradition and the classical Greek past. Earlier Greek religious practices, including paganism, survived in some areas into late antiquity and the Middle Ages.
